brief: On the 2026-08-28 restart the runner failed to launch a worker three times in a row (#34, #35, #36: 1–2 s, 0 tokens, rc=1, model '<synthetic>') and each failure BURNED a brief: run-loop.sh pops the brief before the worker starts, and on rc≠0 it backs off and pops the next one. Three planned briefs were destroyed without a worker ever reading them, and runlog/stall count the rows as ordinary failed iterations, so the dashboard reports 'src moved 7/10' for a run that shipped 7/7. Make a launch failure (rc≠0 with 0 tokens / no raw stream, or elapsed under ~30 s) leave the brief claimed and re-issue it on the next loop, and make stall.mjs and build-stats.mjs exclude such rows from verdict counts the way they already exclude manager rows. Second, smaller: motion.mjs sums a shower's rises and falls into one `jumps` figure, but only a FALL is the bug it exists for — split them so the night cell is attributable (was c62).
successLooksLike: Simulating a launch failure (run the loop with a claude stub that exits 1 in 1 s) leaves current-brief.json claimed and RUNLOG.jsonl carries a row with kind 'launch-failed' that stall.mjs --report neither counts as a worker iteration nor as a verdict; the existing #34–36 rows are re-tagged the same way and the report reads shipped=7 for the last 7. motion.mjs prints rises and falls separately with the baseline regenerated.
avoid: Do not touch courtyard.html. Do not delete the three synthetic rows — retag them; the archive is never edited away. Do not make the fix a retry loop inside run_claude: the runner already backs off on failure, the bug is only which brief the retry gets.
